text: Every testing approach this path has relied on so far has been manual — an admin or developer opens a form, clicks through a workflow, and eyeballs whether it still works. The Automated Test Framework, ATF, is ServiceNow's real, built-in answer to that.

ATF is made of two building blocks. A Test Step is one small, reusable action — opening a form, setting a field, checking a result. A Test is a sequence of Test Steps, run in order, simulating one real scenario start to finish. ATF ships with the platform itself, stored and versioned the same way an Incident or a Business Rule record is, with no external tool or marketplace plugin required.

Course 6 spent an entire course on low-code customization — Business Rules, Client Scripts, UI Policies, Flows. Every one of those can affect behavior far outside the form where it was written, with no syntax error to flag the conflict. That breakage usually surfaces weeks later, as a support ticket, not as an obvious failure at the moment it was introduced.

That's exactly the gap ATF exists to close. Run a Test Suite against a Test environment right before a Change Request is approved, and a regression gets caught while it's still cheap and quiet to fix — not after it's already live in production, breaking something an end user depends on.

This chapter builds that capability in order. Lesson 13 builds a UI Test, composed of steps that simulate a real user clicking through a form. Lesson 14 builds a server-side Test that exercises logic directly, with no UI involved at all. Lesson 15 covers grouping Tests into Suites and running them automatically on a schedule.
ATF's two building blocks — Test Steps and Tests — are the foundation for everything else in this chapter. Next up: building a real UI Test, step by step.
